title: Vendor-neutral DDIL test and conformance harness for tactical software (link emulation, multi-node TAK/CoT sync scoring, pre-Jailbreak API contract tests, TAK plugin RBAC/audit conformance)
problem: Small vendors, prime integration teams and program-office T&E cells have no reproducible, vendor-neutral way to prove before a live event how a tactical application behaves over 1 Mbps to 1 kbps links, partitions and reconnect storms, or whether it conforms to the government-baselined TAK/CoT and NGC2 interfaces and the Army AO's RBAC/audit expectations, so integration and resilience are still proven at expensive in-person events (Operation Jailbreak, Ivy Sting, NetModX, Radio Rodeo).

user.exact_role: Integration and test engineer at a small sensor/vehicle/app vendor preparing for a Jailbreak-series sprint or NGC2 onboarding; prime T&E engineer (Team Anduril / Team Lockheed data-layer or app leads); government network T&E engineer at DEVCOM C5ISR Center, ATEC or the APG/Huntsville software integration labs; TAK plugin developer submitting through the TAK.gov pipelines
user.echelon: Program office, prime and vendor engineering (pre-fielding); indirectly brigade/division units whose exercises absorb the failures
organization_examples: Anduril and Lockheed Martin NGC2 team-lead T&E cells
ATEC and the Huntsville / Aberdeen software integration labs
TAK Product Center third-party pipeline users

current_workflow: 1. Vendor builds a TAK plugin, CoT feed or Lattice SDK integration against documentation and a free vendor sandbox (Lattice Sandboxes) or a self-hosted TAK Server with no link degradation.
2. Vendor and team lead do ad hoc lab tests on an office LAN; bandwidth limits, partitions and reconnect behaviour are rarely scripted.

3. Integration is proven at an in-person event: Operation Jailbreak (Fort Carson, May 2026, ~600 people, 55-80 firms), Ivy Sting / Lightning Surge iterations, or a C5ISR Center Radio Rodeo / NetModX slot.

4. Failures (firewall surprises, undocumented APIs, lag under denied conditions, missing access control and audit logging) are found live and 'fixed in almost real time' by industry engineers during the exercise.

5. Government labs (C5ISR Center, ATEC, APG/Huntsville SILs, Army Software Factory validation of jailbroken interfaces) then harden and validate the capability using their own emulation infrastructure.
6. The next vendor, unit or sprint repeats the cycle; results are not published as reusable, comparable metrics.
current_solution: Government-owned emulation and test infrastructure (DEVCOM C5ISR Center laboratory DDIL effects used in the March-April 2026 Radio Rodeo; NetModX persistent experimentation; ATEC support to Jailbreak; APG and Huntsville software integration labs); government-sponsored open-source emulators NRL EMANE and CORE (with Adjacent Link SRW/WNW waveform ports); commercial network emulators (Keysight EXata / JNE, Apposite, iTrinegy, Linux tc/netem); platform-owner sandboxes (Anduril Lattice Sandboxes, free with unlimited API calls); TAK Server's own takcl test framework and the TAK.gov third-party signing pipeline; generic API contract-test tooling (OpenAPI/protobuf validators, Pact-style contract tests); and, for the DDIL data-load modelling ask, the Army SBIR topic A254-019 selected Assured Information Security's GRUNTS through xTechIgnite 2025.
failure: The pieces exist separately and are owned by parties who have no incentive to publish neutral, comparable scores: link emulation is a government or commercial-appliance product, API sandboxes are platform-owner products, conformance validation is a government lab function, and no one offers a small vendor a single self-hosted run that says 'your feed and plugin survive a 30-minute partition at 4 kbps, reconcile without duplicate tracks, pass the TAK/CoT and Lattice schema contracts, and emit AO-visible audit events' before the sprint date.

evidence.claim: Army SBIR topic A254-019 'Generative AI Enabled Tactical Network' (issued 2025-02-05, proposals due 2025-03-26, Phase I up to $250,000 for 6 months) asks for a modelling and simulation environment that generates realistic threat/blue/logistics tactical data streams and uses AI to simulate limited bandwidth producer-to-consumer to model a DDIL environment for NGC2; award eligibility was restricted to xTechIgnite prize winners. This is the only public solicitation naming DDIL tactical-network test/simulation tooling as a deliverable, and it is a $250k Phase I, not a certification-harness buy.
evidence.source_title: Generative AI Enabled Tactical Network - Army SBIR|STTR Program; HigherGov mirror A254-019; SBIR.gov topic 11775
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: xTechIgnite 2025 selected up to 24 winners ($10,000 each, eligible to submit Phase I or Direct-to-Phase-II SBIR proposals 2025-06-12 to 2025-07-09); the Topic 2 (Generative AI-enabled Tactical Network) winner listed is Assured Information Security, Inc. with 'GRUNTS' (Generative Realistic Utility for Network Testing and Simulation). The one solicited demand signal for DDIL network test tooling is therefore already assigned to an established SBIR firm; a prize/Phase I selection is not evidence of deployment.
evidence.source_title: xTech Winners - xTechSearch (Army xTech program); xTechIgnite competition page
evidence.label: FACT

The government already owns and operates a DDIL emulation lab for NGC2 vendors.

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Because the pieces are already owned by parties for whom they are a means, not a product: link emulation is free government-sponsored software (NRL EMANE/CORE) or a mature commercial appliance market (Keysight EXata/JNE, Apposite, iTrinegy) sold to labs and primes; the API-side test environment is given away by the platform owner (Anduril Lattice Sandboxes, free, unlimited calls) because it grows its ecosystem; TAK's signing pipeline is free and government-run; and conformance/validation of jailbroken interfaces is a statutory-style government function performed by ATEC, C5ISR Center and the APG/Huntsville software integration labs. The one solicited piece of DDIL test tooling (A254-019 GRUNTS) was routed through xTechIgnite to an established SBIR performer (Assured Information Security). What remains for a startup is the scoring/scenario layer that stitches these together for small vendors - useful, but a low-price, episodic B2B purchase that never becomes a mandated acceptance gate unless a government body designates it, and no evidence shows one intends to.
technical_wedge: An open-source, self-hosted 'DDIL bench': (1) a scenario runner that drives Linux tc/netem or EMANE/CORE link profiles from 1 Mbps to 1 kbps with scripted partitions and reconnect storms across roughly 10 containerised ATAK-CIV / TAK Server nodes (later Ditto SDK and Lattice SDK adapters); (2) a scorer that reports time-to-arrival of priority CoT objects, duplicate or conflicting objects after reconnect, link saturation on reconnect and a reconcile-log audit; (3) a contract-test pack that validates a vendor's CoT/TAK Server Mission API and public Lattice protobuf/OpenAPI usage from a capture or spec; (4) an ATAK plugin conformance module that exercises a plugin with synthetic roles and tagged data and emits an RBAC matrix, audit-event coverage and SBOM as a signed, machine-readable (OSCAL-style) bundle. The only proprietary asset would be the scenario library and scoring rubric, which a platform owner or government lab can replicate.

mvp.what: Dockerised TAK DDIL bench: 8-10 ATAK-CIV emulator/TAK Server nodes behind netem (or EMANE/CORE) profiles, a YAML scenario language for link profiles and partition schedules, a scorer producing an HTML/JSON report, plus a contract-test CLI for CoT/TAK Mission API and public Lattice schemas and an ATAK plugin RBAC/audit conformance module.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes: run three public TAK plugins and a synthetic MAVLink/CoT sensor feed through a 30-minute 4 kbps partition-and-reconnect scenario and show comparable scored reports; run the plugin conformance module against an open-source ATAK plugin and emit a signed OSCAL-style results bundle.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That an independent, reproducible score reveals behaviours (arrival order, duplicates after reconnect, link saturation, missing audit events) that vendors and team leads currently discover only at Jailbreak/Ivy Sting, and that at least one vendor and one government or prime T&E engineer will treat the report as pre-event evidence.

data_requirement.what: Synthetic CoT/TAK traffic and mission data; public Lattice SDK schemas (buf.build) and TAK Server API documentation; representative DDIL link profiles (bandwidth, latency, loss, partition schedules); ideally recorded traces from real tactical radios and exercise networks for realism.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Synthetic traffic, public schemas and generic link profiles: yes, today, by both founders. Real PoR radio traces, SRW/WNW EMANE waveform models and exercise network captures: no - these are distribution-controlled or CUI/ITAR-adjacent and require a government sponsor and U.S.-person handling (constraint for counsel, not a legal determination). Realism of the harness therefore plateaus at 'generic DDIL' unless a lab adopts it.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, trivially for their own ecosystems: Anduril already gives away Lattice Sandboxes and could add link-degradation profiles and a conformance report in a release; TAK Product Center already ships a test framework and controls what 'conformant' means; Ditto can publish its own DDIL benchmark; C5ISR Center and ATEC already run the government labs. None of them needs to build a neutral cross-vendor scorer, and that is the only thing they would not build.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: REJECT as a venture. The startup's only defensible claim is impartiality across TAK, Lattice and Ditto, which has value only if a government body (Army CTO/AO, C5ISR Center, TAK Product Center) designates the harness or its report as accepted evidence; no public signal suggests that, and the government has instead built and staffed its own labs and validation steps. A neutral open-source bench can still be a useful credibility asset and a small paid readiness service.

regulatory_burden.explanation: The harness runs on public code (ATAK-CIV, TAK Server, EMANE/CORE, netem), public schemas and synthetic data, with no ATO, CDS or classified dependency to build or sell to vendors. Burden rises to medium-high only if it must ingest PoR radio traces, distribution-controlled waveform models or CUI ICDs, or be adopted inside a government lab boundary.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: The Indonesian founder can build and demonstrate the open-core product as described (INFERENCE from EAR99-type software on public inputs; counsel should confirm and screen dependencies such as EMANE waveform ports). They cannot count toward SBIR ownership/control, cannot be the technical lead on AFWERX-style SBIR work, and should be walled off by a technology control plan from any controlled inputs. This is a constraint description, not a legal determination.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Network-condition and partition testing of offline-first mobile and IoT apps has commercial analogues (public safety / FirstNet apps, maritime, mining, disaster response, retail edge), but generic chaos-engineering and network-emulation tools already serve them; the TAK-specific scoring and AO-style conformance bundle have little commercial pull.

defensibility.explanation: Scenario libraries and scoring rubrics are replicable by any platform owner or lab in weeks; there is no data, accreditation or interface ownership. Defensibility would come only from a government designation of the report as accepted evidence, which is not evidenced. Rated LOW.

why_now: Three things changed: (1) the Army made integration a recurring event series with named dates (Operation Jailbreak May 2026, Falcon Fury, Ivy Sting/Lightning Surge iterations) so 50-80 vendors per event now have a pre-sprint deadline; (2) the NGC2 common data baseline (2026-06), the API Marketplace (2026-05) and the public Lattice SDK schemas made 'conformance' concrete and testable for the first time; (3) DARPA FLUID and the Army's A254-019 topic publicly defined the DDIL regime (1 Mbps to 1 kbps) and admitted the Army lacks a modelling environment for data delivery under it. Against this, the government also stood up its own labs (Radio Rodeo, persistent NetModX, ATEC/SIL hardening) in the same window, which is why the change creates a need but not a purchasable product.
killer_risk: Test and conformance of NGC2/TAK software is a government-owned function that the Army is resourcing itself (C5ISR Center DDIL labs, ATEC and the APG/Huntsville software integration labs, Army Software Factory validation, free TAK signing) on top of free government-sponsored emulators (NRL EMANE/CORE) and free platform sandboxes (Lattice Sandboxes); the only solicited demand for DDIL test tooling was a $250k Phase I already routed to an established SBIR firm. A vendor-neutral harness therefore has no requirement owner, no program office, no budget line and no vehicle, and its residual buyers (small vendors before a sprint) form an episodic, low-price market that drifts into consultancy.

But allied test-and-evaluation is likewise a government/prime function with its own labs and commercial emulators, budgets are smaller and slower, and the Lattice/NGC2 conformance half is U.S.-specific. Allies widen the lab-tool niche without changing its ceiling.
